newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech March ind output falls 2.5 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Czech March ind output falls 2.5 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Real industrial output in the Czech Republic in March contracted 2.5 percent, year-on-year, putting first quarter real output down 4.2 percent compared to the first three months of 1996, the statistical bureau (CSU) said on Monday.

It added that average industrial monthly wages grew, in nominal terms, 14.6 percent, year-on-year, in March, after 11.4 percent growth in February. The CSU also said that real construction output for March grew by 2.0 percent, year-on- year, after a 1.6 percent year-on-year contraction in February.
The CSU added that industrial sales for March, in real terms, eased by 0.8 percent, year-on-year.
NOTE. The average nominal industrial wage in March was 9,222 crowns compared with 9,222 in February. The March index of real industrial wages was up 7.3 percent.

In January, the CSU changed its methodology for calculating industrial production. The new methodology excludes multiple calculation of semi-finished products, resources, and other materials and commodities, which were included in output data at every stage under the old method measuring the gross value of all goods produced.
The new index measures output changes by units, weight or other measurements, of the total of 1,304 products out of 879 product groups consisting of one or more similar products.

The product groups's output indices are placed in sectors, using weighting equal to their weight in the respective industrial sector. The overall index is calculated from weighted changes in the sectoral indices.
